text: I’ll trace the frozen AX initialization path and the pinned-task contract, focusing on whether the recorded run exercised an owner or ordering violation.

The recorded IRQ setup already matches CPU0, so the generic create-then-pin gap is not enough to explain this failure. I’m checking whether the first queued initialization is ordered after affinity assignment, and whether any earlier owner-sensitive work can be inspected locally.

The first explicit `wifi_init_process` request is constructed only after the task-creation wrapper has returned successfully. That places its LMAC initialization after affinity assignment. The remaining uncertain window is the ROM task’s entry prefix; I’m checking the IRQ call path and available ROM coverage before closing that boundary.
